# YouTube Full

Complete YouTube toolkit via [TranscriptAPI.com](https://transcriptapi.com). Everything in one skill.

## Setup

If `$TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY` is not set, read [references/auth-setup.md](references/auth-setup.md) and follow the instructions there to get and store the key.

## Required Headers

Every request needs two headers:

- **Authorization:** `Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY`
- **User-Agent:** your agent's name and version if known (e.g. `HermesAgent/0.11.0`, `ClaudeCode/1.0`). Version is optional — agent name alone is fine. Do not omit this header or send a bare default — Cloudflare will return a 403 (error code 1010) and block the request.

## API Reference

Full OpenAPI spec: [transcriptapi.com/openapi.json](https://transcriptapi.com/openapi.json) — consult this for the latest parameters and schemas.

## Transcript — 1 credit

```bash
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/transcript\
?video_url=VIDEO_URL&format=text&include_timestamp=true&send_metadata=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"
```

| Param               | Required | Default | Values                          |
| ------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `video_url`         | yes      | —       | YouTube URL or 11-char video ID |
| `format`            | no       | `json`  | `json`, `text`                  |
| `include_timestamp` | no       | `true`  | `true`, `false`                 |
| `send_metadata`     | no       | `false` | `true`, `false`                 |

**Response** (`format=json`):

```json
{
  "video_id": "dQw4w9WgXcQ",
  "language": "en",
  "transcript": [{ "text": "...", "start": 18.0, "duration": 3.5 }],
  "metadata": { "title": "...", "author_name": "...", "author_url": "..." }
}
```

## Video Info & Metadata

```bash
# Free — languages available for the transcript endpoint
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/info?video_url=VIDEO_URL" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"

# 1 credit — rich metadata (views, likes, description, duration, tags)
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/video/metadata\
?video_url=VIDEO_URL&include=details,related" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"
```

`include` on `video/metadata` accepts `details` and/or `related`. Naming: `/video/metadata` was previously `/video/info` — the old path still works but is deprecated.

## Search — 1 credit/page

```bash
# Videos
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/search?q=QUERY&type=video&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"

# Channels, playlists, or movies
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/search?q=QUERY&type=channel&limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"
```

| Param   | Required | Default | Validation                                     |
| ------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `q`     | yes      | —       | 1-200 chars                                      |
| `type`  | no       | `video` | `video`, `channel`, `playlist`, `movie`         |
| `sort`  | no       | `relevance` | `relevance`, `views` (first page only)      |
| `upload_date` | no | —       | `hour`, `today`, `week`, `month`, `year` (videos, first page) |
| `duration` | no    | —       | `short`, `medium`, `long` (videos, first page)  |
| `features` | no    | —       | e.g. `hd,subtitles,cc` (first page)             |
| `limit` | no       | `20`    | 1-50                                             |

## Channels

All channel endpoints accept `channel` — an `@handle`, channel URL, or `UC...` channel ID. No need to resolve first.

### Resolve handle — FREE

```bash
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/channel/resolve?input=@TED" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"
```

Response: `{"channel_id": "UC...", "resolved_from": "@TED"}`

### Latest 15 videos — FREE

```bash
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/channel/latest?channel=@TED" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"
```

Returns exact `viewCount` and ISO `published` timestamps.

### Channel feed (videos/shorts/streams) — 1 credit/page

```bash
# First page (100 items, tab defaults to "videos")
curl -s "https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/channel/videos?channel=@NASA&tab=videos" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: YourAgent/1.0"

# Most-viewed first (channel Videos tab, ~30 items)
curl -s
[truncated]
```

## Best Practices

- Use `channel_latest` (free) before `get_transcript` to check if a video is new
- Cache transcripts in your workflow — each `get_transcript` call costs 1 credit
- Use `search_in_channel` when you already know the channel to avoid broad search noise
- Prefer `get_playlist_videos` for course or lecture series — cheaper than searching by query
- Don't batch-transcribe entire channels unless the user explicitly requested it
- Don't use `search_youtube` when you already have the video URL — jump straight to `get_transcript`

## Limitations

- This skill does not replace environment-specific validation, testing, or expert review.
- Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, or safety boundaries are missing.
- Transcripts are available only when YouTube has captions (manual or auto-generated). Some videos have no captions.
- API key is required for paid usage beyond the free 100-credit tier. Get one at transcriptapi.com.
- Rate limits apply: 200 RPM on Monthly plan, 300 RPM on Annual. Contact support for higher limits.

## Security & Safety Notes

- This skill makes HTTPS API calls to `transcriptapi.com`. No local data is written.
- The API key is stored in the agent's credential store, not in this SKILL.md.
- No shell commands, no binary execution, no local system mutation. Risk level: `safe`.

## Common Pitfalls

- **Problem:** `yt-dlp` fails when the agent runs on a cloud server.  
  **Solution:** This is exactly the use case for `youtube-full`. The API routes through TranscriptAPI's infrastructure a

---
name: video-downloader
description: Download YouTube videos with customizable quality and format options, or use natural-language requests for single, batch, or playlist downloads.
---

# Video Downloader

Download YouTube videos with control over quality, format, and output location.

## When to Use

- Downloading YouTube videos for offline viewing, editing, or archival
- Saving educational content, conference talks, or webinars
- Downloading your own content from platforms
- Getting audio-only MP3 files

## CLI Procedure

Use the bundled script when available:

```bash
python scripts/download_video.py "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID"
```

This downloads the video in best available quality as MP4 to `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` by default.

### Quality

Use `-q` or `--quality`:

- `best` (default)
- `1080p`
- `720p`
- `480p`
- `360p`
- `worst`

Example:

```bash
python scripts/download_video.py "URL" -q 720p
```

### Format

Use `-f` or `--format` for video downloads:

- `mp4` (default)
- `webm`
- `mkv`

Example:

```bash
python scripts/download_video.py "URL" -f webm
```

### Audio Only

Use `-a` or `--audio-only` to download MP3 audio:

```bash
python scripts/download_video.py "URL" -a
```

### Output Directory

Use `-o` or `--output` to change the destination:

```bash
python scripts/download_video.py "URL" -o /path/to/directory
```

## Natural-Language Usage

You can also request downloads in plain language:

- "Download this YouTube video: https://youtube.com/watch?v=..."
- "Download this video in 1080p quality"
- "Download the audio from this YouTube video as MP3"
- "Download all videos from this YouTube playlist: [URL]"
- "Download these 5 YouTube videos: 1. [URL] 2. [URL] ..."

## yt-dlp Installation

- If `yt-dlp` is on your `PATH`, it is used.
- Otherwise, the script may create a local virtualenv at `video-downloader/.venv`, install `yt-dlp` there, and run that binary.
- If venv creation or install fails, install globally, for example: `pipx install yt-dlp`, `brew install yt-dlp`, or your OS package manager.

## Supported URLs

- HTTPS only; `http://` links are rejected.
- YouTube hosts only: `youtube.com` and subdomains such as `www`, `m`, `music`, `youtu.be`, and `youtube-nocookie.com` (including `www`).

## Important Notes

- Downloads are saved to `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` by default.
- Video filename is automatically generated from the video title.
- Only single videos are downloaded by default; playlists are skipped unless the skill explicitly supports batch or playlist downloads.
- Higher quality videos may take longer to download and use more disk space.
- Only download videos you have permission to download; respect copyright laws and platform terms of service.

## Conflicts

- Playlist support: Prat011/awesome-llm-skills supports batch and playlist downloads, while davepoon/buildwithclaude, ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills, and composio-community/awesome-codex-skills state that only single videos are downloaded and playlists are skipped by default.
- yt-dlp installation: davepoon/buildwithclaude says the script does not install packages into system Python and uses a local .venv if yt-dlp is not on PATH, while ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills and composio-community/awesome-codex-skills say the script automatically installs yt-dlp if not present.

leader.instruction:
# Literature Search

## Overview

This skill searches academic literature using one or more of the following approaches, depending on the user's needs and available tools:

1. **Multi-source CLI/API search** (LeoYeAI style): Use the `lit` CLI or TypeScript API to search arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed, CrossRef, DBLP, CORE, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, Unpaywall, and Web Search. Supports query expansion, PDF download, and smart sorting.
2. **Agent-driven web search with verification** (brycewang-stanford style): Search field-appropriate databases (Google Scholar, Web of Science, JSTOR, Semantic Scholar, and field-specific sources), web-fetch every candidate paper to verify title, authors, year, and DOI, curate results, and output a markdown table.
3. **Valyu semantic search** (FreedomIntelligence style): Use the Valyu API to search PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv with natural language queries, returning full-text content and images.

## When to Use

- The user asks to search for papers, review literature, find references, verify a paper exists, or build a bibliography.
- The user needs comprehensive coverage across multiple academic sources.
- The user needs PDFs of open-access papers.
- The user needs full-text content from biomedical and preprint sources.

## Conflicts

- **LeoYeAI/openclaw-master-skills** uses a local CLI (`lit`) and TypeScript API with a wide range of sources and PDF download capabilities. It does not require per-paper web verification or a specific markdown table output.
- **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** mandates web-fetching every candidate paper to verify existence and DOI, curating results, and outputting a markdown table with specific columns. It does not use a local CLI or the Valyu API.
- **FreedomIntelligence/OpenClaw-Medical-Skills** requires a Valyu API key and uses the Valyu semantic search API for PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv. It returns full-text content and images, which the other two do not.

## Steps

### 1. Determine the Search Approach

- If the user needs PDFs or a wide range of sources, use the **Multi-source CLI/API** approach.
- If the user needs verified citations for a bibliography, use the **Agent-driven web search with verification** approach.
- If the user needs full-text content from biomedical and preprint sources, use the **Valyu semantic search** approach.

### 2. Multi-source CLI/API Search (LeoYeAI style)

- Use the `lit` CLI or TypeScript API.
- Specify sources, limit, and sort criteria.
- Optionally download PDFs.

### 3. Agent-driven Web Search with Verification (brycewang-stanford style)

- Identify the research field from context.
- Choose field-appropriate databases.
- Search with specific queries.
- Web-fetch every candidate paper to verify title, authors, year, and DOI.
- Curate results and output a markdown table.

### 4. Valyu Semantic Search (FreedomIntelligence style)

- Ensure a Valyu API key is available.
- Use the Valyu API to search PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv.
- Process results using `jq` or the Valyu SDK.

## Output Format

- **Multi-source CLI/API**: JSON or markdown with paper metadata and optional PDF paths.
- **Agent-driven web search**: Markdown table with columns: `Authors (Year)`, `Title`, `Venue`, `DOI`, `Relevance`.
- **Valyu semantic search**: JSON with `success`, `type`, `query`, `result_count`, `results` (including `title`, `url`, `content`, `source`, `relevance_score`, `images`), and `cost`.

## Verification

- For the agent-driven approach, every paper in the final list must be web-fetched and verified.
- For the other approaches, verify that the search was successful and that the results are relevant.

leader.instruction:
# Write

This skill handles two distinct workflows based on context:

## 1. Authoring Agent Skills
Use this when creating or revising `SKILL.md` files.
- **Trigger:** The frontmatter `description` must clearly state what the skill does and when to use it.
- **Token Economy:** Keep the main file short. Use `references/` for long docs and `scripts/` for fragile operations.
- **Procedures:** Write imperative rules and decision points, not essays. Match the procedure to the deliverable's shape.
- **Validation:** Test the skill on a fresh agent run to ensure predictability.

## 2. Drafting Academic Papers
Use this when drafting sections of a research paper.
- **Context:** Read existing drafts, notes, and bibliography before writing.
- **Routing:** Select the section (intro, strategy, results, conclusion, abstract) based on user input.
- **Standards:**
  - Introduction: 1000-1500 words, hook to roadmap.
  - Results: 800-1500 words, effect sizes with units.
  - Abstract: 100-150 words, question to implication.
- **LaTeX Conventions:** Use `\citet{}` for textual and `\citep{}` for parenthetical citations. Use `booktabs` for tables.
- **Quality Check:** Ensure all equations are labeled, citations exist in the bibliography, and no banned hedging phrases are used.
- **Humanizer:** Apply a pass to strip AI-specific patterns (e.g., 'delve', 'leverage', rule-of-three) before finalizing.

# Academic Pipeline — Full Academic Research Workflow Orchestrator

A lightweight orchestrator that manages the complete academic pipeline from research exploration to final manuscript. It does not perform substantive work — it only detects stages, recommends modes, dispatches skills, manages transitions, and tracks state.

## Routing Discipline

**Step 0 — Escape hatch check:** If the user's first message begins with `[direct-mode]`, strip the prefix and skip directly to explicit-intent handling. The token is not passed to the dispatched agent.

**Step 1 — Explicit clear intent:** If the user invokes a specific skill via slash command or unambiguous trigger keyword, route directly.

**Step 2 — Cross-phase materials:** If the user provides artifacts spanning ≥ 2 pipeline phases without naming a specific skill, clarify. List candidate workflows as options.

**Step 3 — Ambiguous intent:** If no artifacts or clear request are provided, clarify.

## Pipeline Stages

| Stage | Name | Skill / Agent Called | Deliverables |
|-------|------|---------------------|--------------|
| 1 | RESEARCH | `deep-research` | RQ Brief, Methodology, Bibliography, Synthesis |
| 2 | WRITE | `academic-paper` | Paper Draft |
| 2.5 | INTEGRITY | `integrity_verification_agent` | Integrity verification report + corrected paper |
| 3 | REVIEW | `academic-paper-reviewer` | 5 review reports + Editorial Decision + Revision Roadmap |
| 4 | REVISE | `academic-paper` | Revised Draft, Response to Reviewers |
| 3' | RE-REVIEW | `academic-paper-reviewer` | Verification review report |
| 4' | RE-REVISE | `academic-paper` | Second revised draft (if needed) |
| 4.5 | FINAL INTEGRITY | `integrity_verification_agent` | Final verification report (100% pass required) |
| 5 | FINALIZE | `academic-paper` | Final Paper (MD, DOCX, PDF) |
| 6 | PROCESS SUMMARY | orchestrator | Paper creation process record (MD + PDF) |

## State Machine

1. **Stage 1 RESEARCH** -> user confirmation -> Stage 2
2. **Stage 2 WRITE** -> user confirmation -> Stage 2.5
3. **Stage 2.5 INTEGRITY** -> PASS -> Stage 3 (FAIL -> fix and re-verify, max 3 rounds)
4. **Stage 3 REVIEW** -> Accept -> Stage 4.5 / Minor|Major -> Stage 4 / Reject -> Stage 2 or end
5. **Stage 4 REVISE** -> user confirmation -> Stage 3'
6. **Stage 3' RE-REVIEW** -> Accept|Minor -> Stage 4.5 / Major -> Stage 4'
7. **Stage 4' RE-REVISE** -> user confirmation -> Stage 4.5
8. **Stage 4.5 FINAL INTEGRITY** -> PASS (zero issues) -> Stage 5 (FAIL -> fix and re-verify)
9. **Stage 5 FINALIZE** -> MD + DOCX -> ask about LaTeX -> confirm -> PDF -> Stage 6
10. **Stage 6 PROCESS SUMMARY** -> generate process record MD -> LaTeX -> PDF -> end

## Opt-in Features

- Set `ARS_PASSPORT_RESET=1` to promote checkpoints to context-reset boundaries.
- Set `ARS_AUDIT_ARTIFACT_GATE=1` to enable the Audit Artifact Gate for external audit scripts.

## Conflicts

- **Imbad0202/academic-research-skills** includes the routing core and audit/reset flags but does not explicitly list Stage 6 in the provided text.
- **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** explicitly lists Stage 6 (Process Summary) and the full state machine but lacks the routing core and audit/reset flags.

# Paper Polish

## Overview
This skill polishes and verifies an existing academic manuscript. It supports two modes: a language-level polish that preserves the author's meaning, and a structured LaTeX proofreading and verification pass. Choose the mode based on the user's request and the manuscript format.

## When to Use
- The user asks to polish, proofread, check, or improve an existing draft.
- The user wants to remove AI tone, fix awkward wording, or translate a Chinese manuscript into publishable English.
- The user has a LaTeX paper and wants a comprehensive check of titles, consistency, citations, formatting, and structural coherence.

## When NOT to Use
- No prose exists yet and the user wants a section written from an idea.
- The user wants the paper's logic skeleton planned from scratch.
- The user wants a full reviewer-style audit beyond polishing and proofreading.

## Mode 1: Language-Level Polish

### Overriding Rule: Stay Faithful to the Author's Meaning
- Never silently make an edit that changes scientific meaning.
- Do not strengthen or weaken conclusions, turn correlations into causal claims, or drop qualifiers without explicit author confirmation.
- Do not delete or heavily compress arguments; suggest cuts instead.
- Pure language edits (grammar, word order, smoother phrasing with identical meaning) are safe to make freely.
- Edits that might touch meaning must be flagged for the author to confirm.

### Never Fabricate Content
- Add no data, numbers, equations, results, citations, or method names not in the original.
- If a passage lacks evidence, leave a parenthetical note to the author instead of inventing content.

### Conservative by Default
- Prefer the small edit over the big one, and no edit over the small one.
- Do not "improve" hedged language into stronger claims.
- If a structural rewrite is needed, stop and let the author choose between light polish and deep rewrite.

### Polishing Pass
1. Understand the passage's purpose and role in the paper.
2. Identify whether the problem is surface grammar or structural logic.
3. Edit within the faithfulness rule, applying section-specific conventions.
4. Deliver clean polished text and briefly state the main edits, flagging any that might have touched meaning.

### Section Conventions
- Introduction: positions the work.
- Methods: enables reproduction.
- Results: states observations in past tense.
- Discussion: interprets and hedges.
- Abstract: miniature paper.
- Title: searchable and restrained.

### AI-Tone Removal and Chinese-to-English Rewriting
- Strip AI-generated phrasing and make the prose idiomatic.
- For Chinese drafts, rewrite into submission-quality English while preserving the author's meaning and hedging.

## Mode 2: LaTeX Proofreading and Verification

### Initialization
1. Receive the paper directory path.
2. Scan the directory to identify the main LaTeX file, bibliography file, results directory, and any PDF with original tables/figures.
3. Read all files into context.
4. Present an inventory and confirm with the user before proceeding.

### Interaction Rule
For every issue found in every check:
1. Present the issue clearly (original vs. proposed change, or finding).
2. Ask the user: "Accept this change? (yes/no/edit)"
3. Wait for the user's response before proceeding to the next issue.
4. If "yes", apply the change.
5. If "no", skip and move to the next issue.
6. If "edit" or alternative text is provided, apply the user's version.
7. After all issues in a check are resolved, announce completion and move to the next check.

### The 19 Checks
Run these checks in order:
1. Section and Subsection Titles: Optimize titles for academic rigor; no colons.
2. Table and Figure Titles: Optimize captions for academic rigor; no colons.
3. Internal Consistency of Arguments: Check for contradictory or inconsistent claims across sections.
4. Introduction Logic and Flow: Ensure tight flow from motivation to findings to contributions.
5. Storyline Coherence: Evaluate overall storyline; suggest moving non-essential tables to appendix.
6. Theoretical Tension in Introduction Motivation: Ensure motivation establishes competing forces or perspectives that make the research question interesting ex ante.
7. Concise Results Reporting: Check that results are reported concisely and without redundancy.
8. Cross-Section Repetition: Identify and reduce unnecessary repetition across sections.
9. Em-Dash Usage: Standardize em-dash usage per style guide.
10. Auxiliary-Text-to-Footnote Conversion: Convert auxiliary text to footnotes where appropriate.
11. Citation Formatting: Verify citation format and consistency.
12. Reference List Completeness: Ensure all in-text citations appear in the bibliography and vice versa.
13. Equation Numbering and Referencing: Check equation numbering and cross-references.
14. Table and Figure Numbering: Verify sequential numbering and correct references.
15. Spelling and Grammar: Run a final pass for spelling and grammar errors.
16. Formatting Consistency: Check for consistent use of bold, italics, and other formatting.
17. Margin and Layout Issues: Identify any layout problems that may affect compilation or readability.
18. Compilation Warnings: Review LaTeX compilation log for warnings and errors.
19. Final Read-Through: Perform a final holistic read for flow and clarity.

## Conflicts
- HKUSTDial/Supervisor-Skills::skills/paper-polish/SKILL.md does not mandate a per-issue interactive approval loop, while brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills::skills/67-econfin-workflow-toolkit/paper-polish/SKILL.md requires it for every issue in every check.
- HKUSTDial/Supervisor-Skills::skills/paper-polish/SKILL.md includes Chinese-to-English rewriting and AI-tone removal, which are not part of the brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills::skills/67-econfin-workflow-toolkit/paper-polish/SKILL.md procedure.
- brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills::skills/67-econfin-workflow-toolkit/paper-polish/SKILL.md includes LaTeX-specific checks (e.g., em-dash usage, auxiliary-text-to-footnote conversion, compilation warnings) that are absent from the HKUSTDial/Supervisor-Skills::skills/paper-polish/SKILL.md procedure.

# Academic Paper Reviewer

Simulates a complete international journal peer review process: automatically identifies the paper's field, dynamically configures 4 card-backed reviewer identities, and adds a fixed Devil's Advocate as the fifth execution seat. A separate editorial synthesizer produces the structured Editorial Decision and Revision Roadmap.

## Quick Start

```
Review this paper: [paste paper or provide file]
```

Output:
1. Automatically identifies the paper's field and methodology type
2. Dynamically configures the specific identities and expertise of 5 reviewers
3. 5 independent review reports (each from a different perspective)
4. 1 Editorial Decision Letter + Revision Roadmap

## Trigger Conditions

**English**: review paper, peer review, manuscript review, referee report, review my paper, critique paper, simulate review, editorial review, calibrate reviewer, reviewer calibration, measure reviewer accuracy

### Non-Trigger Scenarios

| Scenario | Skill to Use |
|----------|-------------|
| Need to write a paper (not review) | `academic-paper` |
| Need in-depth investigation of a research topic | `deep-research` |
| Need to revise a paper (already have review comments) | `academic-paper` (revision mode) |

### Quick Mode Selection Guide

| Your Situation | Recommended Mode |
|----------------|-----------------|
| Need comprehensive review (first submission) | full |
| Checking if revisions addressed comments | re-review |
| Quick quality assessment (15 min) | quick |
| Focus only on methods/statistics | methodology-focus |
| Want to learn by doing (guided review) | guided |
| Measure reviewer accuracy | calibration |

## Agent Team (7 Agents)

| # | Agent | Role | Phase |
|---|-------|------|-------|
| 1 | `field_analyst_agent` | Analyzes the paper's field, dynamically configures 5 reviewer identities | Phase 0 |
| 2 | `journal_fit_reviewer_agent` | Journal-Fit Reviewer — journal fit, originality, overall quality | Phase 1 |
| 3 | `methodology_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 1 — research design, statistical validity, reproducibility | Phase 1 |
| 4 | `domain_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 2 — literature coverage, theoretical framework, domain contribution | Phase 1 |
| 5 | `perspective_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 3 — cross-disciplinary connections, practical impact, challenging fundamental assumptions | Phase 1 |
| 6 | `devils_advocate_reviewer_agent` | Devil's Advocate — core argument challenges, logical fallacy detection, strongest counter-arguments | Phase 1 |
| 7 | `editorial_synthesizer_agent` | Synthesizes all reviews, identifies consensus and disagreements, makes editorial decision | Phase 2 |

## Orchestration Workflow (3 Phases)

```
User: "Review this paper"
     |
=== Phase 0: FIELD ANALYSIS & PERSONA CONFIGURATION ===
     |
     +-> [field_analyst_agent] -> Reviewer Configuration Card (x5)
         - Reads the complete paper
         - Identifies: primary discipline, secondary discipline, research paradigm, methodology type, target journal tier, paper maturity
         - Dynamically generates specific identities for 5 reviewers
     |
     ** Presents Reviewer Configuration to user for confirmation (adjustable) **
     |
=== Phase 1: PARALLEL MULTI-PERSPECTIVE REVIEW ===
     |
     |-> [journal_fit_reviewer_agent] -> Journal-Fit Review Report
     |   - Journal fit, originality, significance, relevance to readership
     |   - Sets the review tone
     |
     |-> [methodology_reviewer_agent] -> Methodology Review Report
     |   - Research design rigor, sampling strategy, data collection
     |   - Analysis method selection, statistical validity, effect sizes
     |   - Reproducibility, data transparency
     |
     |-> [domain_reviewer_agent] -> Domain Review Report
     |   - Literature review completeness, theoretical framework appropriateness
     |   - Academic argument accuracy, incremental contribution to the field
     |   - Missing key references
     |
     |-> [perspective_reviewer_agent] -> Perspective Review Report
     |   - Cross-disciplinary connections and borrowing opportunities
     |   - Practical applications and policy implications
     |   - Broader social or ethical implications
     |
     +-> [devils_advocate_reviewer_agent] -> Devil's Advocate Report
         - Core argument challenges (strongest counter-arguments)
         - Logical fallacy detection
     |
=== Phase 2: EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS ===
     |
     +-> [editorial_synthesizer_agent] -> Editorial Decision + Revision Roadmap
```

## Routing Discipline

**Step 0 — Escape hatch check (before any classification):** If the user's first message begins with `[direct-mode]` (case-insensitive byte-0 token, optionally preceded by whitespace/newlines that are stripped on parse), record this fact, strip the prefix and surrounding whitespace from the message, and skip directly to **Step 1 explicit-intent handling** on the stripped content. The literal `[direct-mode]` is NOT passed through to the dispatched agent. If the stripped message itself has no clear skill named, Step 1 falls through to Step 3 clarification. When the token is honored and the named agent or skill needs inputs the message does not supply, read that agent's or skill's file and ask for what it requires, in its terms. A `[direct-mode]` token after any other non-whitespace character is not the escape hatch, even when the message asks to skip questions: classify the message through Steps 1-3 as if the token were absent, and do not forward the token. Without the byte-0 token, naming an agent is not explicit intent: such a message goes through Steps 1-3 like any other, so cross-phase materials still get Step 2 clarification.

Otherwise, classify the user's input:

1. **Explicit clear intent** — user invokes a specific skill via `/ars-*` slash command, or uses an unambiguous trigger keyword that maps to a single skill (e.g., "lit-review this", "review my paper", "draft an abstract"):
   → Route directly; no clarification, no orchestrator detour.
   → The request stays explicit when the mode's usual input is absent or a word in it has other everyday senses. A revision request with no reviewer comments is revision mode's "feel certain sections need improvement" case, and "revisar artículo" is the reviewer's trigger. Route to that mode and let the mode handle what is missing; do not reopen the choice of workflow.

2. **Cross-phase materials detected** — user provides artifacts spanning ≥ 2 pipeline phases without naming a specific skill (e.g., pre-written abstract + pre-collected literature; full draft + reviewer comments + bibliography):
   → **Clarify**. Do NOT auto-route to a single-phase agent. List candidate workflows as a-d options in markdown body (NOT via AskUserQuestion tool).
   → Reason: clarification is the safest action when materials don't unambiguously identify intent.

3. **Ambiguous intent, no materials** — user provides no artifacts and no clear request:
   → Clarify per the intent clarification protocol.

**Screening boundary (sr-screener):** a request to screen records the user already has (database exports, pasted abstracts, full-text PDFs) against a review's eligibility criteria, or to build a screening protocol, pilot the screening, adjudicate screening conflicts, audit exclusions, or report the selection counts, routes to `sr-screener`. A request to write a literature review, or to run a systematic review, meta-analysis, or PRISMA report, does not route to `sr-screener`. Screening starts only when the user asks for it: `deep-research` `systematic-review` mode may mention `sr-screener`, but never hands over to it automatically.

**Anti-pattern:** Receiving ambiguous cross-phase materials and silently auto-routing to a single-phase agent based on which phase the materials "look closest to." This bypasses orchestrator-level reconciliation.

## Conflicts

- **Imbad0202/academic-research-skills** uses a **Journal-Fit Reviewer** as the first seat; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** uses an **Editor-in-Chief** as the first seat.
- **Imbad0202/academic-research-skills** includes a **calibration mode** and a **routing/escape-hatch protocol**; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** omits both and instead includes a **Quick Start** and **trigger/non-trigger table**.

# Academic Paper — Academic Paper Writing Agent Team

A general-purpose academic paper writing tool — 12-agent pipeline covering all disciplines.

## Routing Discipline

**Step 0 — Escape hatch check:** If the user's first message begins with `[direct-mode]`, strip the prefix and skip to Step 1.

**Step 1 — Explicit clear intent:** If the user invokes a specific skill or uses an unambiguous trigger keyword, route directly.

**Step 2 — Cross-phase materials:** If the user provides artifacts spanning multiple phases without naming a skill, clarify intent by listing candidate workflows.

**Step 3 — Ambiguous intent:** If no artifacts or clear request are provided, clarify per the intent clarification protocol.

## Execution Flow

1. **Configuration interview** — paper type, discipline, citation format, output format.
2. **Literature search** — systematic search strategy, source screening.
3. **Architecture design** — paper structure, outline, word count allocation.
4. **Argumentation construction** — claim-evidence chains, logical flow.
5. **Full-text drafting** — section-by-section draft, register adjustment.
6. **Citation compliance + bilingual abstract** (parallel).
7. **Peer review** — five-dimension scoring, revision suggestions.
8. **Output formatting** — LaTeX/DOCX/PDF/Markdown.

## Agent Team (12 Agents)

1. `intake_agent` — Configuration interview.
2. `literature_strategist_agent` — Search strategy design.
3. `structure_architect_agent` — Paper structure selection.
4. `argument_builder_agent` — Argument construction.
5. `draft_writer_agent` — Section-by-section full draft writing.
6. `citation_compliance_agent` — Citation compliance.
7. `abstract_writer_agent` — Bilingual abstract generation.
8. `peer_reviewer_agent` — Simulated peer review.
9. `revision_coach_agent` — Revision guidance.
10. `format_converter_agent` — Output formatting.
11. `disclosure_agent` — AI disclosure.
12. `rebuttal_auditor_agent` — Rebuttal audit.

## Writing Quality Features

- **Style Calibration:** Learn the author's writing voice from past papers.
- **Writing Quality Check:** Context-sensitive writing diagnostics applied during self-review.

---
name: ai-ml
---

# AI/ML Skill Routing

Select the routing mode that matches the user's request, then follow the corresponding steps.

## Production AI/ML Workflow

Use this mode when the user is building LLM applications, RAG systems, AI agents, ML pipelines, AI-powered features, or AI observability.

1. Select only the phases needed for the requested product. This workflow does not authorize delegation, hosted calls, deployment, background jobs, or external messages.
2. Read the actual selected skill and available tool schema.
3. Define task-level quality, retrieval/source checks, data permissions, latency/currency limits, and failure recovery before implementation.
4. Verify each used capability in the target environment. Unchecked checklist items are not completed because an instruction exists.

### Phase 1: AI Application Design
- Skills: ai-product, ai-engineer, ai-agents-architect, llm-app-patterns
- Actions: define AI use cases, choose models, design system architecture, plan data flows, define success metrics.

### Phase 2: LLM Integration
- Skills: llm-application-dev-ai-assistant, llm-application-dev-langchain-agent, llm-application-dev-prompt-optimize, gemini-api-dev
- Actions: select LLM provider, set up API access, implement prompt templates, configure model parameters, add streaming support, implement error handling.

### Phase 3: RAG Implementation
- Skills: rag-engineer, rag-implementation, embedding-strategies, vector-database-engineer, similarity-search-patterns, hybrid-search-implementation
- Actions: design data pipeline, choose embedding model, set up vector database, implement chunking strategy, configure retrieval, add reranking, implement caching.

### Phase 4: AI Agent Development
- Skills: autonomous-agents, autonomous-agent-patterns, crewai, langgraph, multi-agent-patterns, computer-use-agents
- Actions: design agent architecture, define agent roles, implement tool integration, set up memory systems, configure orchestration, add human-in-the-loop.

### Phase 5: ML Pipeline Development
- Skills: ml-engineer, mlops-engineer, machine-learning-ops-ml-pipeline, ml-pipeline-workflow, data-engineer
- Actions: design ML pipeline, set up data processing, implement model training, configure evaluation, set up model registry, deploy models.

### Phase 6: AI Observability
- Skills: langfuse, manifest, evaluation, llm-evaluation
- Actions: set up tracing, configure logging, implement evaluation, monitor performance, track costs, set up alerts.

### Phase 7: AI Security
- Skills: prompt-engineering, security-scanning-security-sast
- Actions: implement input validation, add output filtering, configure rate limiting, set up access controls, monitor for abuse, implement audit logging.

### Checklists
- LLM Integration: API keys secured, rate limiting configured, error handling implemented, streaming enabled, token usage tracked.
- RAG System: data pipeline working, embeddings generated, vector search optimized, retrieval accuracy tested, caching implemented.
- AI Agents: agent roles defined, tools integrated, memory working, orchestration tested, error handling robust.
- Observability: tracing enabled, metrics collected, evaluation running, alerts configured, dashboards created.
- Quality Gates: all AI features tested, performance benchmarks met, security measures in place, observability configured, documentation complete.

## Research AI/ML Skill Index

Use this mode when the user needs ML experiments, model training, deep learning, NLP, computer vision, paper reproduction, benchmarks, or AI research workflows.

Select the skill matching the user's need, then read its SKILL.md.

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| ai-agent-papers-guide | Curated 2024-2026 AI agent research papers collection |
| ai-model-benchmarking | Benchmark AI models across 60+ academic evaluation suites and metrics |
| anomaly-detection-papers-guide | Industrial anomaly detection methods and benchmark papers |
| autonomous-agents-papers-guide | Daily-updated collection of autonomous AI agent papers |
| computer-vision-guide | Apply computer vision research methods, models, and evaluation tools |
| deep-learning-papers-guide | Annotated deep learning paper implementations with code walkthroughs |
| dl-transformer-finetune | Build transformer fine-tuning plans for classification and generation |
| domain-adaptation-papers-guide | Comprehensive collection of domain adaptation research papers |
| generative-ai-guide | Curated guide to generative AI covering LLMs and diffusion models |
| graph-learning-papers-guide | Conference papers on graph neural networks and graph learning |
| huggingface-api | Search and discover ML models, datasets, and Spaces on Hugging Face |
| huggingface-inference-guide | Run NLP and CV model inference via Hugging Face free-tier API |
| keras-deep-learning | Build and debug deep learning models with Keras and TensorFlow backend |
| kolmogorov-arnold-networks-guide | Papers and tutorials on KAN learnable activation networks |
| llm-evaluation-guide | Evaluate and benchmark large language models for research applications |
| llm-from-scratch-guide | Build a ChatGPT-like LLM from scratch using PyTorch step by step |
| ml-pipeline-guide | Build and deploy reproducible production ML pipelines for research |
| nlp-toolkit-guide | NLP analysis with perplexity scoring, burstiness, and entropy metrics |
| npcpy-research-guide | All-in-one Python library for NLP, agents, and knowledge graphs |
| prompt-engineering-research | Systematic prompt engineering methods for AI-assisted academic research workflows |
| pytorch-guide | Avoid common PyTorch mistakes and apply robust training patterns |
| pytorch-lightning-guide | PyTorch Lightning framework for scalable model training and research |
| reinforcement-learning-guide | Reinforcement learning fundamentals, algorithms, and research |
| responsible-ai-guide | Resources for trustworthy, fair, and ethical AI research |
| tensorflow-guide | TensorFlow best practices for tf.function, GPU memory, and deployment |
| transformer-architecture-guide | Guide to Transformer architectures for NLP and computer vision |
| vmas-simulator-guide | Vectorized multi-agent reinforcement learning simulator |

## Conflicts
- sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills defines a multi-phase production workflow with explicit constraints on delegation, hosted calls, deployment, background jobs, external messages, and checklist completion. brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills provides a flat research skill index with a simple select-and-read instruction and no such constraints.

leader.instruction:
# Auto Research

This skill covers three distinct workflows. Select the one that matches the user's request.

## Workflow A: Local Parameter Optimization (dzhng/skills)

1. Recover the research state: objective, incumbent artifact, regression set, hypothesis queue, and remaining budget.
2. Clarify success criteria: evaluator, metric, baseline, and required improvement. Define the smallest useful loop with one cheap task.
3. Establish the active task's baseline. Run the unchanged artifact once or reuse a compatible recorded result.
4. Plan a small hypothesis batch. List distinct explanations of the bottleneck and the parameters that could test them.
5. Test one hypothesis on the active task. Change one conceptual factor, record the prediction, and compare observation with prediction.
6. Combine and promote compatible winners. Check interactions and remove one change at a time when attribution is unclear.

## Workflow B: Delegated Strategic Research (huytieu/COG-second-brain)

1. Read .claude/skills/auto-research/SKILL.md and execute it exactly as written.
2. Follow .agents/rules/cog.md.
3. Where the playbook delegates to a .claude/agents/<name> worker, invoke .agents/agents/<name>.md via invoke_subagent instead.

## Workflow C: External Research with Explicit Consent (sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills)

1. Propose the research boundary: state the source, exact query or redacted prompt, whether any local text would leave the machine, and the likely cost. Wait for user approval.
2. Research: after approval, use web search or a browser session the user has explicitly selected and authorized. Do not install packages automatically or access browser cookies, other tabs, saved passwords, or sessions.
3. Present: distill findings into concise options with sources.
4. Await Approval: do not write code until the user says "go ahead" or picks an option.
5. Implement: once approved, execute with confidence.

### Conflicts

- dzhng/skills::skills/engineering/auto-research/SKILL.md runs local experiments without requiring external web search or third-party consultation.
- huytieu/COG-second-brain::.agents/skills/auto-research/SKILL.md does not define the procedure itself; it delegates to .claude/skills/auto-research/SKILL.md.
- sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills::plugins/agentic-awesome-skills-claude/skills/auto-research/SKILL.md requires explicit user approval before any web search or ChatGPT submission and forbids sending context, files, or browser state without consent.

---
name: auto-review-loop-llm
description: Autonomous research review loop using any OpenAI-compatible LLM API. Configure via llm-chat MCP server or environment variables. Trigger with "auto review loop llm" or "llm review".
argument-hint: "[topic-or-scope]"
allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Agent, Skill
---

# Auto Review Loop (Generic LLM): Autonomous Research Improvement

> 🔒 **Do not wrap this skill in `/loop`, `/schedule`, or `CronCreate`.** It already loops internally (review → fix → re-review), feeding each round's prior-round summary into the next review prompt. An external timer re-enters from the top each tick, dropping accumulated context and firing the verdict on wall-clock time instead of on artifact change. Schedule the external wait that precedes it, not the verdict.

Autonomously iterate: review → implement fixes → re-review, until the external reviewer gives a positive assessment or MAX_ROUNDS is reached.

## Context: $ARGUMENTS

## Constants

- MAX_ROUNDS = 4
- POSITIVE_THRESHOLD: **Conflicts** — wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep uses score >= 6/10 AND verdict ∈ {"ready", "almost"}; brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills uses score >= 6/10 OR verdict contains "accept", "sufficient", "ready for submission". Choose the threshold that matches your project's review policy.
- REVIEW_DOC: **Conflicts** — wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep uses `review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md` (fall back to `./AUTO_REVIEW.md` for legacy projects); brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills uses `AUTO_REVIEW.md` in project root.

## LLM Configuration

This skill uses **any OpenAI-compatible API** for external review via the `llm-chat` MCP server.

### Configuration via MCP Server (Recommended)

Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "llm-chat": {
      "command": "/usr/bin/python3",
      "args": ["/Users/yourname/.claude/mcp-servers/llm-chat/server.py"],
      "env": {
        "LLM_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "LLM_BASE_URL": "https://api.deepseek.com/v1",
        "LLM_MODEL": "deepseek-chat"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Supported Providers

| Provider | LLM_BASE_URL | LLM_MODEL |
|----------|--------------|-----------|
| **OpenAI** | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `gpt-4o`, `o3` |
| **DeepSeek** | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `deepseek-chat`, `deepseek-reasoner` |
| **MiniMax** | `https://api.minimax.io/v1` | `MiniMax-M3` |
| **Kimi (Moonshot)** | `https://api.moonshot.cn/v1` | `moonshot-v1-8k`, `moonshot-v1-32k` |
| **ZhiPu (GLM)** | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4` | `glm-4`, `glm-4-plus` |
| **SiliconFlow** | `https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1` | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct` |
| **阿里云百炼** | `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` | `qwen-max` |
| **零一万物** | `https://api.lingyiwanwu.com/v1` | `yi-large` |

## API Call Method

**Primary: MCP Tool**

```
mcp__llm-chat__chat:
  prompt: |
    [Review prompt content]
  model: "deepseek-chat"
  system: "You are a senior ML reviewer..."
```

**Fallback: curl**

```bash
curl -s "${LLM_BASE_URL}/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLM_API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "${LLM_MODEL}",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior ML reviewer..."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "[review prompt]"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 4096
  }'
```

## State Persistence (Compact Recovery)

Persist state to `REVIEW_STATE.json` after each round. **Conflicts** — wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep uses `review-stage/REVIEW_STATE.json` (fall back to `./REVIEW_STATE.json` for legacy projects); brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills uses `REVIEW_STATE.json` in project root.

```json
{
  "round": 2,
  "status": "in_progress",
  "last_score": 5.0,
  "last_verdict": "not ready",
  "pending_experiments": [],
  "timestamp": "2026-03-15T10:00:00"
}
```

**Write this file at the end of every Phase E** (after documenting the round).

**On completion**, set `"status": "completed"`.

## Workflow

### Initialization

1. **Check `REVIEW_STATE.json`** for recovery
2. Read project context and prior reviews
3. Initialize round counter

### Loop (up to MAX_ROUNDS)

#### Phase A: Review

**If MCP available:**
```
mcp__llm-chat__chat:
  system: "You are a senior ML reviewer (NeurIPS/ICML level)."
  prompt: |
    [Round N/MAX_ROUNDS of autonomous review loop]

    [Full research context: claims, methods, results, known weaknesses]
    [Changes since last round, if any]

    1. Score this work 1-10 for a top venue
    2. List remaining critical weaknesses (ranked by severity)
    3. For each weakness, specify the MINIMUM fix
    4. State clearly: is this READY for submission? Yes/No/Almost

    Be brutally honest. If the work is ready, say so clearly.
```

**If MCP NOT available:**
```bash
curl -s "${LLM_BASE_URL}/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLM_API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "${LLM_MODEL}",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior ML reviewer (NeurIPS/ICML level)."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "[Full review prompt]"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 4096
  }'
```

#### Phase B: Parse Assessment

**CRITICAL: Save the FULL raw response** verbatim. Then extract:
- **Score** (numeric 1-10)
- **Verdict** ("ready" / "almost" / "not ready")
- **Action items** (ranked list of fixes)

**STOP**: If the POSITIVE_THRESHOLD condition is met (see Conflicts above).

#### Phase C: Implement Fixes

Priority: metric additions > reframing > new experiments

#### Phase D: Wait for Results

Monitor remote experiments

#### Phase E: Document Round

Append to `REVIEW_DOC`:

```markdown
## Round N (timestamp)

### Assessment (Summary)
- Score: X/10
- Verdict: [ready/almost/not ready]
- Key criticisms: [bullet list]

### Reviewer Raw Response

<details>
<summary>Click to expand full reviewer response</summary>

[Paste the COMPLETE raw response here — verbatim, unedited.]

</details>

### Actions Taken
- [what was implemented/changed]

### Results
- [experiment outcomes, if any]

### Status
- [continuing to round N+1 / stopping]
```

**Write `REVIEW_STATE.json`** with current state.

### Termination

1. Set `REVIEW_STATE.json` status to "completed"
2. Write final summary

## Key Rules

- **Large file handling**: If the Write tool fails due to file size, immediately retry using Bash (`cat << 'EOF' > file`) to write in chunks. Do NOT ask the user for permission — just do it silently.
- **Anti-hallucination citations**: When adding references, NEVER fabricate BibTeX. Use DBLP → CrossRef → `[VERIFY]` chain. Do NOT generate BibTeX from memory.
- Be honest about weaknesses
- Implement fixes BEFORE re-reviewing
- Document everything
- Include previous context in round 2+ prompts
- Prefer MCP tool over curl when available

## Prompt Template for Round 2+

```
mcp__llm-chat__chat:
  system: "You are a senior ML reviewer (NeurIPS/ICML level)."
  prompt: |
    [Round N/MAX_ROUNDS of autonomous review loop]

    [Full research context: claims, methods, results, known weaknesses]
    [Changes since last round, if any]
    [Previous round's assessment summary and action items]

    1. Score this work 1-10 for a top venue
    2. List remaining critical weaknesses (ranked by severity)
    3. For each weakness, specify the MINIMUM fix
    4. State clearly: is this READY for submission? Yes/No/Almost

    Be brutally honest. If the work is ready, say so clearly.
```

## Conflicts

- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** vs **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills**: POSITIVE_THRESHOLD uses AND with verdict set {ready, almost} vs OR with verdict keywords {accept, sufficient, ready for submission}.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** vs **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills**: REVIEW_DOC path is `review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md` (with legacy fallback) vs `AUTO_REVIEW.md` in project root.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** vs **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills**: REVIEW_STATE.json path is `review-stage/REVIEW_STATE.json` (with legacy fallback) vs `REVIEW_STATE.json` in project root.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** includes an explicit anti-wrapping constraint (no /loop, /schedule, CronCreate); **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** does not.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Skill; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Agent, Skill.

leader.instruction:
# Autoresearch

This skill covers two distinct autonomous optimization workflows. Determine which mode is requested based on the user's intent.

## Mode 1: Content Optimization (Marketing)
Use when optimizing landing pages, email sequences, ad copy, or other conversion-focused content.

1. **Intake:** Parse the source content and identify optimizable elements (headlines, CTAs, etc.).
2. **Panel Setup:** Define a 5-expert scoring panel (e.g., CMO, Skeptical Founder, CRO, Copywriter, CEO).
3. **Optimization Loop:**
   - Generate 10 variants per element.
   - Batch-score all variants with the panel in a single API call.
   - Keep the top 3 variants.
   - Evolve the top 3 into new variants for the next round.
   - Repeat until a score threshold (e.g., 80/100) is met or 3 rounds are complete.
4. **Cross-Breeding:** Combine the best elements from each category into a final optimized version.
5. **Output:** Save the optimized content, experiment log, and optimization report.

## Mode 2: Autonomous Research Orchestration (Science)
Use when starting a research project, running autonomous experiments, or managing a multi-hypothesis research effort.

1. **Bootstrap:** Clarify the research question, search literature, and form initial hypotheses.
2. **Workspace Setup:** Create a structured directory for state, logs, findings, literature, code, data, and experiments.
3. **Two-Loop Execution:**
   - **Inner Loop:** Run rapid experiment iterations with clear optimization targets. Record results and learnings.
   - **Outer Loop:** Periodically synthesize results, identify patterns, update findings, and steer research direction.
4. **Finalize:** Write the research paper and produce a final presentation.

## Conflicts
- **ericosiu/ai-marketing-skills** focuses on simulated expert scoring of marketing copy variants.
- **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** focuses on autonomous scientific research orchestration with a two-loop experiment/synthesis architecture.

name: research-pipeline
description: "Full end-to-end research pipeline: from a broad research direction through idea discovery, experiments, and review all the way to a polished paper PDF. Use when user says \"全流程\", \"full pipeline\", \"从找idea到投稿\", \"end-to-end research\", or wants the complete autonomous research lifecycle."

# Full Research Pipeline: Idea → Experiments → Submission

> ⏱ **External cadence: non-judgmental heartbeat only.** An overnight `/loop` / `CronCreate` heartbeat may wake, detect a **stalled** phase (no progress, dead process, blocked on a freed resource) and **nudge** it forward — it may NEVER decide the work is good (paper good enough, proof holds, claim supported). Every such verdict stays on its own skill's internal cadence and terminates in the cross-model jury. A heartbeat may say "keep going," never "good enough." See `shared-references/external-cadence.md` (overnight-pipeline rule + stall detection & forced structural pivot). At heartbeat startup, touch the run state first each tick and register this run with the watchdog `loop` type (so a silent death surfaces as STALE); unregister on completion. The watchdog only detects — it never acquits. Each tick also record the new-finding count via the `iteration_log.py` helper (resolve through the canonical `.aris/tools → tools → $ARIS_REPO/tools → $ARIS_REPO/tools via ~/.aris/repo` chain, integration-contract §2; warn-and-skip if unresolved): `python3 "$ITER_LOG" note <root> <run_id> <phase> <n>`. On the returned `pivot=structural` (stale ≥ 2) the nudge must change a STRUCTURAL constraint and pick an untried direction; on `pivot=human` (stale ≥ 4) flag for attention. Counting only — never a quality verdict.

End-to-end autonomous research workflow for: **$ARGUMENTS**

## Optional formal proof route

Before creating an experimental run, route theorem-centered requests for Lean to `/lean-formalize` and report its actual proof result. Run the experimental stages below when the task includes empirical research. In a mixed project, use Lean for a user-requested formal proof or a specific mathematical obligation whose formal verification would materially help; return its checked scope and remaining obligations to the research summary and applicable proof audit. Ordinary mathematics stays in the existing theory skills. Difficulty alone does not make Lean mandatory, and a formal sublemma does not establish an empirical claim.

## Constants

- **AUTO_PROCEED = true** — When `true`, every selection checkpoint is informational: report the choice and continue in the same turn. When `false`, ask for explicit user confirmation and end the turn at the checkpoint.
- **ARXIV_DOWNLOAD = false** — When `true`, `/research-lit` downloads the top relevant arXiv PDFs during literature survey. When `false` (default), only fetches metadata via arXiv API. Passed through to `/idea-discovery` → `/research-lit`.
- **HUMAN_CHECKPOINT = false** — When `true`, the auto-review loops (Stage 3) pause after each round's review to let you see the score and provide custom modification instructions before fixes are implemented. When `false` (default), loops run fully autonomously. Passed through to `/auto-review-loop`.
- **REVIEWER_DIFFICULTY = medium** — How adversarial the reviewer is. `medium` (default): standard MCP review. `hard`: adds reviewer memory + debate protocol. `nightmare`: GPT reads repo directly via `codex exec` + memory + debate. Passed through to `/auto-review-loop`.
- **CODE_REVIEW = true** — GPT-6-Astra xhigh reviews experiment code before deployment. Catches logic bugs before wasting GPU hours. Set `false` to skip. Passed through to `/experiment-bridge`.
- **BASE_REPO = false** — GitHub repo URL to use as base codebase. When set, `/experiment-bridge` clones the repo first and implements experiments on top of it. When `false` (default), writes code from scratch or reuses existing project files. Passed through to `/experiment-bridge`.
- **COMPACT = false** — When `true`, generates compact summary files for short-context models and session recovery. Passed through to `/idea-discovery` and `/experiment-bridge`.
- **AUTO_WRITE = false** — When `true`, automatically invoke Workflow 3 (`/paper-writing`) after Stage 4. `VENUE` is needed only when Stage 5 begins — a missing venue defers paper writing; it never blocks Stages 1-4. When `false` (default), Stage 4 generates `NARRATIVE_REPORT.md` and stops — user invokes `/paper-writing` manually.
- **VENUE = (unset)** — Target venue for paper writing; bound only when Stage 5 begins. Options: `ICLR`, `NeurIPS`, `ICML`, `CVPR`, `ACL`, `AAAI`, `ACM`, `IEEE_CONF`, `IEEE_JOURNAL`. No default: a missing venue defers paper writing — it never blocks Stages 1-4 and is never guessed.
- **RENDER_HTML = true** — When `true` (default), auto-render `NARRATIVE_REPORT.md` to HTML at Stage 4 completion via `/render-html`. Uses `--no-review` (this is an internal handoff doc to `/paper-writing`, not a reviewer-facing final artifact — the upstream Stage 3 auto-review loop already cross-model-reviewed the claims). Set `false` to skip, or pass `— render html: false`. **Non-blocking**: if `/render-html` fails or Codex MCP is unavailable, log the failure and continue — the HTML view is a nice-to-have, not a Stage 4 prerequisite.
- **RESUMABLE = true** — When `true` (default), the pipeline records per-stage state to `.aris/runs/<run_id>.json` so a crashed/interrupted run can resume via `/research-pipeline — resume <run_id>` instead of restarting. Stage status splits `done` (executor finished writing) from `accepted` (the stage's cross-model gate / deterministic verifier passed); resume re-validates any `done`-but-unaccepted stage.

> 💡 Override via argument, e.g., `/research-pipeline "topic" — AUTO_PROCEED: false, human checkpoint: true`.

## Overview

This skill chains the entire research lifecycle into a single pipeline:

```
/idea-discovery → implement → /run-experiment → /auto-review-loop → submission-ready
├── Workflow 1 ──┤            ├────────── Workflow 2 ──────────────┤
```

It orchestrates two major workflows plus the implementation bridge between them.

## Pipeline

### Stage 1: Idea Discovery (Workflow 1)

If `RESEARCH_BRIEF.md` exists in the project root, it will be automatically loaded as detailed context (replaces one-line prompt). See `templates/RESEARCH_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md`.

Invoke the idea discovery pipeline:

```
/idea-discovery "$ARGUMENTS"
```

This internally runs: `/research-lit` → `/idea-creator` → `/novelty-check` → `/research-review`

**Output:** `IDEA_REPORT.md` with ranked, validated, pilot-tested ideas.

**🚦 Gate 1 — Human Checkpoint:**

After `IDEA_REPORT.md` is generated, **pause and present the top ideas to the user**:

```
📋 Idea Discovery complete. Top ideas:

1. [Idea 1 title] — Pilot: POSITIVE (+X%), Novelty: CONFIRMED
2. [Idea 2 title] — Pilot: WEAK POSITIVE (+Y%), Novelty: CONFIRMED
3. [Idea 3 title] — Pilot: NEGATIVE, eliminated

Recommended: Idea 1. Shall I proceed with implementation?
```

**If AUTO_PROCEED=false:** Wait for user confirmation before continuing. The user may:
- **Approve an idea** → proceed to Stage 2.
- **Pick a different idea** → proceed with their choice.
- **Request changes** (e.g., "combine Idea 1 and 3", "focus more on X") → update the idea prompt with user feedback, re-run `/idea-discovery` with refined constraints, and present again.
- **Reject all ideas** → collect feedback on what's missing, re-run Stage 1 with adjusted research direction. Repeat until the user commits to an idea.
- **Stop here** → save current state to `IDEA_REPORT.md` for future reference.

**If AUTO_PROCEED=true:** Present the top ideas, wait 10 seconds for user input. If no response, auto-select the #1 ranked idea (highest pilot signal + novelty confirmed) and proceed to Stage 2. Log: `"AUTO_PROCEED: selected Idea 1 — [title]"`.

> ⚠️ **This gate waits for user confirmation when AUTO_PROCEED=false.** When `true`, it auto-selects the top idea after presenting results. The rest of the pipeline (Stages 2-4) is expensive (GPU time + multiple review rounds), so set `AUTO_PROCEED=false` if you want to manually choose which idea to pursue.

### Stage 2: Implementation

Once the user confirms which idea to pursue:

1. **Read the idea details** from `IDEA_REPORT.md` (hypothesis, experimental design, pilot code)

2. **Implement the full experiment**:
   - Extend pilot code to full scale (multi-seed, full dataset, proper baselines)
   - Add proper evaluation metrics and logging (wandb if configured)
   - Write clean, reproducible experiment scripts
   - Follow existing codebase conventions

3. **Code review**: Before deploying, do a self-review:
   - Are all hyperparameters configurable via argparse?
   - Is the random seed fixed and controllable?
   - Are results saved to JSON/CSV for later analysis?
   - Is there proper logging for debugging?

### Stage 3: Deploy Experiments (Workflow 2 — Part 1)

Deploy the full-scale experiments:

```
/run-experiment [experiment command]
```

**What this does:**
- Check GPU availability on configured servers
- Sync code to remote server
- Launch experiments in screen sessions with proper CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
- Verify experiments started successfully

**Monitor progress:**

```
/monitor-experiment [server]
```

Wait for experiments to complete. Collect results.

### Stage 4: Auto Review Loop (Workflow 2 — Part 2)

Once initial results are in, start the autonomous improvement loop:

```
/auto-review-loop "$ARGUMENTS — [chosen idea title]"
```

**What this does (up to 4 rounds):**
1. GPT-5.4 xhigh reviews the work (score, weaknesses, minimum fixes)
2. Claude Code implements fixes (code changes, new experiments, reframing)
3. Deploy fixes, collect new results
4. Re-review → repeat until score ≥ 6/10 or 4 rounds reached

**Output:** `AUTO_REVIEW.md` with full review history and final assessment.

### Stage 5: Final Summary

After the auto-review loop completes, write a final status report:

```markdown
# Research Pipeline Report

**Direction**: $ARGUMENTS
**Chosen Idea**: [title]
**Date**: [start] → [end]
**Pipeline**: idea-discovery → implement → run-experiment → auto-review-loop

## Journey Summary
- Ideas generated: X → filtered to [final count]
- Experiments run: [count]
- Review rounds: [count]
- Final score: [score]/10
```

## Conflicts

- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep::skills/research-pipeline/SKILL.md** places the auto-review loop at Stage 3 and treats selection checkpoints as informational when AUTO_PROCEED=true; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills::skills/42-wanshuiyin-ARIS/skills/research-pipeline/SKILL.md** places the auto-review loop at Stage 4 and, when AUTO_PROCEED=true, waits 10 seconds for user input before auto-selecting the top idea.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep::skills/research-pipeline/SKILL.md** includes an external heartbeat/watchdog cadence, a Lean formal-proof route, and a RESUMABLE run-state mechanism; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills::skills/42-wanshuiyin-ARIS/skills/research-pipeline/SKILL.md** omits all of these and instead loads RESEARCH_BRIEF.md and uses /run-experiment and /monitor-experiment as explicit stages.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep::skills/research-pipeline/SKILL.md** lists REVIEWER_DIFFICULTY, CODE_REVIEW, BASE_REPO, COMPACT, AUTO_WRITE, VENUE, RENDER_HTML, and RESUMABLE constants; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills::skills/42-wanshuiyin-ARIS/skills/research-pipeline/SKILL.md** does not.

description: Autonomous multi-round research review loop. Reviews via a configurable backend (Copilot-native, Codex, or manual), implements fixes, and re-reviews until a policy-approved positive assessment or max rounds is reached. Supports state persistence for context-compaction recovery.
argument-hint: "[topic-or-scope]"
allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Skill, Task, mcp__codex__codex, mcp__codex__codex-reply, mcp__manual_review__review, mcp__manual_review__review_reply

# Auto Review Loop: Autonomous Research Improvement

> Do not wrap this skill in /loop, /schedule, or CronCreate. It already loops internally and the reviewer carries round-to-round memory in one threadId. An external timer resets reviewer memory each tick.

Autonomously iterate: review → implement fixes → re-review, until an independent reviewer gives a policy-approved positive assessment or MAX_ROUNDS is reached.

## Context: $ARGUMENTS

## Constants

- MAX_ROUNDS = 4
- POSITIVE_THRESHOLD: score >= 6/10 AND verdict in {"ready", "almost"} — both must hold.
- REVIEW_DOC: review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md (cumulative log). Fall back to ./AUTO_REVIEW.md for legacy projects.
- REVIEWER_MODEL = gpt-6-astra — Default model for the Codex backend. Must be an OpenAI model.
- REVIEWER_BACKEND — With no reviewer directive, start as auto; Step -1 runs a two-call native marker/challenge probe. A bound Copilot CLI root session uses copilot-native; an unbound host keeps codex. Explicit directives (codex, oracle-pro, agy, manual, copilot) bypass the probe.
- OUTPUT_DIR = review-stage/ — All review-stage outputs go here. Create if missing.
- HUMAN_CHECKPOINT = false — When true, pause after each round's review and present score + weaknesses. User can approve, customize, skip, or stop.
- COMPACT = false — When true, read EXPERIMENT_LOG.md and findings.md instead of full logs; append key findings to findings.md after each round.
- REVIEWER_DIFFICULTY = medium — medium (default), hard (adds Reviewer Memory + Debate Protocol), nightmare (adds direct repo read + Adversarial Verification).
- RENDER_HTML = true — When true, auto-render AUTO_REVIEW.md to HTML on loop termination via /render-html with --no-review.

> Nightmare + Manual incompatibility: If REVIEWER_BACKEND = manual and REVIEWER_DIFFICULTY = nightmare, STOP with an error message.

## State Persistence (Compact Recovery)

Long-running loops may hit the context window limit. Persist state to REVIEW_STATE.json after each round:

```json
{
  "round": 2,
  "threadId": "019cd392-...",
  "status": "in_progress",
  "last_score": 5.0,
  "last_verdict": "not ready",
  "pending_experiments": ["screen_name_1"],
  "timestamp": "2026-03-13T21:00:00"
}
```

Write this file at the end of every Phase E. Overwrite each time. On completion, set status to completed.

## Workflow

### Initialization

1. Check for REVIEW_STATE.json:
   - Missing or status=completed: fresh start.
   - status=in_progress and timestamp older than 24 hours: fresh start (delete file).
   - status=in_progress and timestamp within 24 hours: resume. Read state, read AUTO_REVIEW.md, check pending experiments, resume from next round.
2. Read project narrative documents, memory files, and prior review documents. When COMPACT=true and compact files exist, read findings.md + EXPERIMENT_LOG.md instead.
3. Read recent experiment results.
4. Identify current weaknesses and open TODOs.
5. Initialize round counter = 1 (unless recovered).
6. Create/update AUTO_REVIEW.md with header and timestamp.

### Loop (repeat up to MAX_ROUNDS)

#### Phase A: Review

Branch on REVIEWER_BACKEND. For codex, send comprehensive context via mcp__codex__codex with model_reasoning_effort xhigh. Prompt the reviewer to act as a senior ML reviewer, score 1-10, list critical weaknesses ranked by severity, specify minimum fixes, and state readiness. For round 2+, use mcp__codex__codex-reply with the saved threadId.

#### Phase B: Parse Assessment

Save the FULL raw response verbatim. Extract score, verdict, and action items.

STOP CONDITION: If score >= 6 AND verdict in {ready, almost} → stop loop, document final state.

#### Human Checkpoint (if enabled)

If HUMAN_CHECKPOINT=true, present review results and wait for user input. Parse approval, custom instructions, skip, or stop.

#### Phase C: Implement Fixes

Implement the approved fixes. Update code, experiments, and documentation.

#### Phase D: Verify

Verify that fixes address the identified weaknesses.

#### Phase E: Document and Persist

Append the round's review, fixes, and verification to AUTO_REVIEW.md. Write REVIEW_STATE.json. If RENDER_HTML=true and loop is terminating, render to HTML.

## Conflicts

- wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep uses AND for the stop condition; brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills uses OR. The AND form is used here as it is the more conservative and explicitly corrected condition.
- wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep uses gpt-6-astra and a backend probe; brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills uses gpt-5.4 with no probe. The probe and gpt-6-astra are used here as they are the more evolved configuration.
- brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills includes REVIEW_STATE.json persistence; wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep does not. The persistence protocol is included here as it is a material step absent from the other copy.

# Auto Review Loop (MiniMax Version): Autonomous Research Improvement

> 🔒 **Do not wrap this skill in `/loop`, `/schedule`, or `CronCreate`.** It already loops internally (review → fix → re-review), feeding each round's prior-round summary into the next review prompt. An external timer re-enters from the top each tick, dropping accumulated context and firing the verdict on wall-clock time instead of on artifact change — zero new signal, full token cost. Schedule the *external wait that precedes it*, not the verdict.

Autonomously iterate: review → implement fixes → re-review, until the external reviewer gives a positive assessment or MAX_ROUNDS is reached.

## Context: $ARGUMENTS

## Constants

- MAX_ROUNDS = 4
- POSITIVE_THRESHOLD: score >= 6/10 **AND** verdict ∈ {"ready", "almost"} — **both** must hold. Verdict vocabulary is {"ready", "almost", "not ready"}. (Earlier wording used `or` and a stale verdict set; the `AND` form is authoritative.)
- REVIEW_DOC: `review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md` (cumulative log) *(fall back to `./AUTO_REVIEW.md` for legacy projects)*
- REVIEWER_MODEL = `MiniMax-M3` — Model used via MiniMax API

## API Configuration

This skill uses MiniMax API for external review. Two methods are supported:

### Method 1: MCP Tool (Primary)

If `mcp__minimax-chat__minimax_chat` is available, use it:

```
mcp__minimax-chat__minimax_chat:
  prompt: |
    [Review prompt content]
  model: "MiniMax-M3"
  system: "You are a senior machine learning researcher..."
```

### Method 2: curl (Fallback)

If MCP is not available, use curl directly:

```bash
curl -s "https://api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MINIMAX_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "MiniMax-M3",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior ML researcher..."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "[Review prompt]"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 4096
  }'
```

**API Key**: Read from `~/.claude/settings.json` under `env.MINIMAX_API_KEY`, or from environment variable.

**Why MiniMax instead of Codex MCP?** Codex CLI uses OpenAI's Responses API (`/v1/responses`) which is not supported by third-party providers. See: https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/7782

## State Persistence (Compact Recovery)

Long-running loops may hit the context window limit, triggering automatic compaction. To survive this, persist state to `review-stage/REVIEW_STATE.json` after each round:

```json
{
  "round": 2,
  "status": "in_progress",
  "last_score": 5.0,
  "last_verdict": "not ready",
  "pending_experiments": ["screen_name_1"],
  "timestamp": "2026-03-13T21:00:00"
}
```

**Write this file at the end of every Phase E** (after documenting the round). Overwrite each time — only the latest state matters.

**On completion** (positive assessment or max rounds), set `"status": "completed"` so future invocations don't accidentally resume a finished loop.

## Workflow

### Initialization

1. **Check for `review-stage/REVIEW_STATE.json`** *(fall back to `./REVIEW_STATE.json` if not found — legacy path)*:
   - If neither path exists: **fresh start** (normal case)
   - If it exists AND `status` is `"completed"`: **fresh start** (previous loop finished normally)
   - If it exists AND `status` is `"in_progress"` AND `timestamp` is older than 24 hours: **fresh start** (stale state from a killed/abandoned run — delete the file and start over)
   - If it exists AND `status` is `"in_progress"` AND `timestamp` is within 24 hours: **resume**
     - Read the state file to recover `round`, `last_score`, `pending_experiments`
     - Read `review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md` to restore full context of prior rounds *(fall back to `./AUTO_REVIEW.md`)*
     - If `pending_experiments` is non-empty, check if they have completed (e.g., check screen sessions)
     - Resume from the next round (round = saved round + 1)
     - Log: "Recovered from context compaction. Resuming at Round N."
2. Read project narrative documents, memory files, and any prior review documents
3. Read recent experiment results (check output directories, logs)
4. Identify current weaknesses and open TODOs from prior reviews
5. Initialize round counter = 1 (unless recovered from state file)
6. Create/update `review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md` with header and timestamp

### Loop (repeat up to MAX_ROUNDS)

#### Phase A: Review

Send comprehensive context to the external reviewer.

**Check MCP availability first**, then use appropriate method:

**If MCP available (Primary):**
```
Use mcp__minimax-chat__minimax_chat tool with:
- system: "You are a senior machine learning researcher serving as a reviewer for top-tier conferences like NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR. Provide rigorous, constructive feedback."
- prompt: [Full review prompt with context]
- model: "MiniMax-M3"
```

**If MCP NOT available (Fallback):**
```bash
curl -s "https://api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MINIMAX_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "MiniMax-M3",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "system",
        "content": "You are a senior machine learning researcher serving as a reviewer for top-tier conferences like NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR. Provide rigorous, constructive feedback."
      },
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "[Round N/MAX_ROUNDS of autonomous review loop]\n\n[Full research context: claims, methods, results, known weaknesses]\n[Changes since last round, if any]\n[For round 2+: Summary of previous review feedback and what was addressed]\n\nPlease act as a senior ML reviewer (NeurIPS/ICML level).\n\n1. Score this work 1-10 for a top venue\n2. List remaining critical weaknesses (ranked by severity)\n3. For each weakness, specify the MINIMUM fix (experiment, analysis, or reframing)\n4. State clearly: is this READY for submission? Yes/No/Almost\n\nBe brutally honest. If the work is ready, say so clearly."
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 4096
  }'
```

**Note**: Each round is a standalone API call. For round 2+, include the summary of previous reviews and changes in the prompt itself.

#### Phase B: Parse Assessment

**CRITICAL: Save the FULL raw response** from the external reviewer verbatim (store in a variable for Phase E). Do NOT discard or summarize — the raw text is the primary record.

Then extract structured fields:
- **Score** (numeric 1-10)
- **Verdict** ("ready" / "almost" / "not ready")
- **Critical weaknesses** (ranked list)
- **Minimum fixes** (per weakness)

#### Phase C: Implement Fixes

For each critical weakness, implement the minimum fix specified by the reviewer. Prioritize by severity. If a fix requires a new experiment, launch it and add to `pending_experiments`.

#### Phase D: Re-review

If fixes were implemented, proceed to the next round (Phase A). If no fixes were possible, proceed to Phase E.

#### Phase E: Document Round

1. Append the full raw reviewer response to `review-stage/AUTO_REVIEW.md`
2. Update `review-stage/REVIEW_STATE.json` with current round, status, last_score, last_verdict, pending_experiments, and timestamp
3. If the stop condition is met (score >= 6/10 AND verdict in {"ready", "almost"}) or MAX_ROUNDS is reached, set `"status": "completed"` in the state file and exit the loop

## Conflicts

- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** uses POSITIVE_THRESHOLD as score >= 6/10 AND verdict in {"ready", "almost"}; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** uses score >= 6/10 OR verdict contains "accept", "sufficient", "ready for submission". The combined instruction uses the AND form as authoritative.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** stores REVIEW_DOC and REVIEW_STATE.json under `review-stage/` with legacy fallbacks; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** stores them in project root. The combined instruction uses `review-stage/` with fallbacks.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** allows `Skill` but not `Agent`; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** allows `Agent` but not `Skill`. The combined instruction allows both.
- **wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep** includes an explicit warning not to wrap the skill in `/loop`, `/schedule`, or `CronCreate`; **brycewang-stanford/Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills** omits this warning. The combined instruction includes the warning.
